newsitem.title: USA: US rail intermodal up 4.7 pct from year ago - AAR.
newsitem.headline: US rail intermodal up 4.7 pct from year ago - AAR.

text.p: U.S. rail freight as measured in intermodal rose 4.7 percent in the week ended March 8 from the year-ago week, the Association of American Railroads said Thursday.
AAR said intermodal traffic in the week totaled 160,011 trailers and containers, versus 152,798 a year ago. Intermodal does not include carloads.
Carloads in the March 8 week were 341,895, up 0.3 percent from 340,846 in the year-ago week.
Ton-miles rose 1.5 percent to 26.9 billion from 26.5 billion last year. The ton-mile, a measure of freight transportation, equates one ton of freight hauled one mile.

AAR said the biggest carload increases from a year ago were in farm products other than grain, which rose 13.2 percent to 1,281 last week from 1,132 a year ago, and in motor vehicles and equipment, up 10.3 percent to 22,686 loadings from 20,559.

Loadings of lumber and wood products rose 6.8 percent in the week to 5,421 carloads from 5,077 in the year-ago week, while grain mill products rose 6.7 percent to 9,915 carloads from 9,292. Petroleum loadings also increased 3.2 percent to 5,209 carloads from 5,048.
But sharp declines were reported in grain loadings, which fell 13.7 percent to 25,274 from 29,279 a year ago, and in nonmetallic minerals, which decreased 10.4 percent to 8,072 carloads from 9,012.
In the first 10 weeks of 1997, AAR said carloads increased 3.9 percent from the same period last year. Ton-miles were up 4.7 percent and intermodal traffic rose 4.6 percent from the same 1996 period.

AAR also said carloads on Canada's two transcontinental railroads totaled 56,826 in the March 8 week, a 5.2 percent gain from a year ago, while intermodal traffic rose 10.3 percent to 25,483 trailers and containers from last year.
